sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's digital economy monetization is accelerating, with BELI and BUKA benefiting from rising ad spend and e-commerce transaction volumes independent of global tech sentiment.
Local tech valuations remain supported by domestic liquidity and consumption growth, unlike US peers which face higher rate sensitivity and AI capex digestion risk.
Structural winners are platform and software names (IRSX, CYBR) with recurring revenue, while hardware and telecom equipment (2454, WGSH) face margin compression from input costs and FX volatility.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian tech names with local revenue exposure (BELI, IRSX, BUKA) as US tech weakness creates relative outperformance; the +0.92% ID vs -1.87% US spread confirms domestic demand resilience. Favor digital advertising and e-commerce enablers over hardware; trim positions in US-linked semis (2454) and telecom equipment (WGSH) on rate-driven de-rating. Maintain normal signal, add on dips to BELI and IRSX for Q3 earnings momentum.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's coal export demand remains structurally supported by Asian thermal power buildout and China's import appetite, underpinning recurring cash flows for large-cap producers like BUMI.
Downstream processing mandates for nickel and other minerals are driving value-add investments and re-rating potential for mid-cap miners with smelting exposure, as seen in CUAN's momentum.
Domestic energy security policies, including biofuel blending and gas infrastructure expansion, create durable demand tailwinds for local refining and petrochemical players such as INCI and ALKA.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to coal and nickel-linked names (BUMI, CUAN, INCI) on the back of firm thermal coal prices and Indonesia's downstream nickel processing momentum; avoid chasing speculative small caps like SQMI after a 35% spike. Position for Q4 earnings beats and potential dividend announcements, but keep stops tight given US rate volatility.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's renewable buildout is structurally supported by the RUPTL's 75% new-capacity target for renewables, locking in multi-year demand for local EPC and O&M players.
Gas-to-power integration (ESSA, CSAP) is a durable margin driver as LNG spot prices stay elevated, favoring domestic feedstock and captive power contracts.
Climate-tech financing is shifting to IDX-listed vehicles (BREN, CDIA) as green bond issuance and carbon credit monetization create recurring revenue beyond one-off project sales.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in ESSA and CSAP; both are re-rating on firm gas-to-power economics and domestic demand. Rotate out of US-exposed names (BRPT, TPIA) into pure-play ID beneficiaries like CDIA and BREN. Maintain normal exposure; the ID/US divergence widens as local policy tailwinds accelerate project pipelines through Q3.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Premiumization and health-conscious product shifts are driving outsized gains for smaller FMCG players (KKES, COCO) as they capture share from legacy brands in Indonesia's urban centers.
Export-oriented consumer companies (TAPG, ENZO) benefit from resilient global demand and favorable commodity prices, providing a hedge against domestic purchasing-power volatility.
Merger and acquisition speculation, particularly around cash-rich mid-caps (LUCY, BMBL), is a recurring catalyst as foreign and local conglomerates consolidate the fragmented consumer space.
sectors.ai: Buy dips on mid-cap consumer names with strong volume breakouts (KKES, COCO, TAPG) as the sector's relative strength vs. the IDX persists, but trim exposure to laggards like FLMC and WMPP that lack fundamental catalysts. Favor companies with pricing power and export exposure to ride the rupiah stability and domestic demand recovery into Q3.

themes: Indonesia's domestic consumption recovery is outpacing US-linked media exposure, making local entertainment and consumer-service names structurally advantaged over the next 12 months.

Streaming and digital content adoption in Indonesia remains underpenetrated, giving CSMI and similar platforms a multi-year growth runway independent of global ad-cycle swings.
sectors.ai: Buy selectively into PTSP and SINI on momentum, but cap exposure—both are low-float names prone to sharp reversals. Favor CSMI for structural streaming upside and PLAN for tourism recovery leverage. Trim US-linked names like BUVA and FORU given the negative US read-through. Overall, stay WATCH: aggregate gains are ID-driven, so rotate into domestic consumption plays with earnings visibility, not speculative spikes.
